data.narrative:
Atmos Space Cargo is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Sebastian Klaus, Marta Oliveira, Jeffrey Hendrikse, and Christian Grimm, having raised €30M to date. The valuation analysis triangulates against a peer universe of 3 private companies in the same sector and adjacent stages, plus 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) representing the broader Space & Aerospace sector.

Two valuation methods proved applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the €30M total raised as a baseline proxy, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding €60M. Peer-median anchoring across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables—Cowboy Space Corporation ($2.0B, Series B), Aalyria ($1.3B, Series B), and Starcloud ($1.1B, Seed)—produces a median valuation of $1.3B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. Public-comp anchoring was not applicable because the target's revenue remains undisclosed, preventing application of the 27.4x P/S median observed across the six public tickers.

The triangulated valuation range is $51M (low), $680M (median), and $1.5B (high). This wide spread reflects material stage and maturity dispersion within the peer set. Key uncertainties include the target's actual revenue trajectory relative to Series B-stage peers, capital efficiency in executing on cargo missions, and whether current private market valuations in space infrastructure remain sustainable. The peer median of $1.3B should be weighted against execution risk at the Series A stage.
